latestRelease.notes:
🎉 **Release Announcement** 🎉: We are excited to announce the [Cilium 1.20.0](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/releases/tag/v1.20.0) release!

More than **2,660 new commits** have landed in this release, supported by a community of over **1,100 contributors** and more than **24,800 GitHub stars**! 🤩

⚠️ You may need to take action during the upgrade if you use legacy Mutual Authentication, Envoy Go extensions or Kafka-aware policies, the `cilium.io/v2alpha1` `CiliumNodeConfig` API, the libnetwork integration, or a custom CNI configuration. See the [Upgrade Guide](https://docs.cilium.io/en/v1.20/operations/upgrade/#upgrade-notes) for details.

The full changelog can be found [here](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/v1.20/CHANGELOG.md).

Here are some of the highlights:

* ⛩️ **Gateway API**
    * 🚀 **Gateway API v1.6.1**: Cilium moves from Gateway API v1.4 to v1.6.1, bringing support for capabilities that graduated across both upstream releases. ([cilium/cilium#45251](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45251), @youngnick; [cilium/cilium#46827](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46827), [cilium/cilium#47274](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/47274), @arybolovlev)
    * 👥 **Delegate Gateway Listeners**: ListenerSets let application teams attach and manage their own listeners while the platform team retains ownership of the shared Gateway. ([cilium/cilium#46303](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46303), [cilium/cilium#46785](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46785), @asauber)
    * 🔏 **Encrypt Traffic to Backends**: Gateway API `BackendTLSPolicy` support lets operators configure TLS and backend certificate validation for traffic between the gateway and application services. ([cilium/cilium#43045](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43045), @youngnick)
    * 🔀 **TCPRoute and UDPRoute**: Databases, DNS servers, game servers and other non-HTTP services can now be managed through the same Gateway API model as HTTP and gRPC traffic. ([cilium/cilium#46184](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46184), [cilium/cilium#46970](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46970), @eminaktas; [cilium/cilium#47381](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/47381), @arybolovlev)
    * 🔐 **External Authorization**: HTTPRoute requests can now be authenticated and authorized through an external service before they reach the application, using the Gateway API `ExternalAuth` filter from GEP-1494. ([cilium/cilium#45739](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45739), @gauteoh)
    * 🎛️ **More HTTP Traffic Controls**: HTTPRoutes gain native CORS support and additional 303, 307 and 308 redirect codes. `CiliumGatewayClassConfig` can also overwrite, append or preserve the HTTP Server response header. ([cilium/cilium#45924](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45924), @arybolovlev; [cilium/cilium#47232](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/47232), @youngnick; [cilium/cilium#46764](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46764), @xtineskim)
    * ↔️ **Configurable gRPC-Web Translation**: `CiliumGatewayClassConfig` can disable automatic gRPC-web translation for Gateways that need to pass the original traffic through unchanged. Translation remains enabled by default. ([cilium/cilium#45984](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45984), @thorn3r)


* 🚠 **Networking**
    * 🔌 **Extensible Datapath**: Datapath plugins let cloud providers extend or instrument Cilium's eBPF datapath with independently versioned programs, without maintaining a Cilium fork. ([cilium/cilium#45028](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45028), [cilium/cilium#45429](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45429), [cilium/cilium#45558](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45558), [cilium/cilium#46673](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46673), [cilium/cilium#46872](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46872), @jrife)
    * 🚄 **Automatic Netkit Selection**: Set `bpf.datapathMode=auto` to use netkit automatically on supported kernels and fall back to veth on other nodes. The default remains veth. ([cilium/cilium#43062](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43062), @ajmmm)
    * 📤 **Egress Gateway Improvements**: Dual-stack clusters can configure an explicit IPv6 egress IP. IPv4 Egress Gateway traffic also strictly honors the interface selected by the policy, matching the existing IPv6 behavior. ([cilium/cilium#44524](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44524), @yykkibbb; [cilium/cilium#45833](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45833), @julianwiedmann)
    * 🔍 **Better BGP Tooling and Reconciliation**: New Hive shell commands expose route policies and clearer peer output formats. The control plane moves to GoBGP v4.6.1 and optimizes route-policy reconciliation. ([cilium/cilium#45628](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45628), [cilium/cilium#45534](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45534), @martonra; [cilium/cilium#45952](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45952), [cilium/cilium#46928](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46928), @rastislavs)


* 🌐 **IPAM and IP Selection**
    * ☁️ **IPv6 for AWS ENI IPAM (Beta)**: Cilium can now allocate IPv6 prefixes to pods through AWS ENI IPAM, building on the move to the multi-pool allocator. ([cilium/cilium#46756](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46756), [cilium/cilium#46619](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46619), @41ks; [cilium/cilium#45154](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45154), [cilium/cilium#45958](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45958), @HadrienPatte)
    * 🔄 **Migrate to Multi-Pool IPAM**: Existing clusters can move from cluster-pool IPAM to multi-pool IPAM without being rebuilt. ([cilium/cilium#46104](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46104), @pippolo84)
    * 🧭 **Dynamic NodePort Source Addresses**: NodePort can use the kernel FIB to select the preferred source address dynamically before SNATing north-south traffic, on supported kernels. ([cilium/cilium#44625](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44625), @ldelossa)
    * 🔵 **Prefer IPv6 Consistently**: The new top-level `preferIpv6` option applies to both Cilium health probes and Hubble peer communication when IPv4 and IPv6 are available. ([cilium/cilium#45447](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45447), @tibrezus)


* 🕸️ **Services and Cluster Mesh**
    * 📍 **Topology-Aware Service Traffic**: Cilium's service load balancer now supports the Kubernetes `PreferSameZone` and `PreferSameNode` traffic distribution hints. ([cilium/cilium#44771](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44771), @raphink)
    * ⚖️ **Weighted Maglev Backends**: Maglev now honors the `service.cilium.io/weight` annotation on EndpointSlices. A weight of zero drains new connections while allowing existing connections to continue. ([cilium/cilium#46061](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46061), @mhofstetter)
    * 🌉 **More Load-Balancing Options with VXLAN**: Clusters using VXLAN can use per-Service load-balancing mode annotations, including compatible DSR configurations such as IPIP dispatch. ([cilium/cilium#45600](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45600), @brb)
    * 🤖 **Stable MCS API Support**: Cilium's implementation of the Kubernetes Multi-Cluster Services API is now stable and recommended for portable service discovery through ClusterMesh. ([cilium/cilium#45404](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45404), [cilium/cilium#46953](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46953), @MrFreezeex)


* 🔒 **Encryption and Network Policy**
    * 🚇 **Improved Ztunnel Identity Management**: The ztunnel path now supports either an internal certificate authority or SPIRE-issued workload identities, alongside new Prometheus metrics for enrollment and connection health. It transparently encrypts enrolled pod-to-pod connections, including traffic between pods on the same node. ([cilium/cilium#43763](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43763), [cilium/cilium#44275](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44275), [cilium/cilium#44136](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44136), [cilium/cilium#45861](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45861), @nddq; [cilium/cilium#45096](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45096), @gokulMSFT)
    * 🛡️ **Kubernetes ClusterNetworkPolicy (KCNP)**: Cilium now supports the upstream, cluster-scoped policy API, including Admin and Baseline policy tiers alongside namespaced Kubernetes NetworkPolicy. ([cilium/cilium#42338](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/42338), @TheBeeZee; [cilium/cilium#46253](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46253), @aanm)
    * ⛔ **Friendlier IPv6 Policy Denials**: Cilium can return ICMPv6 Destination Unreachable responses when network policy denies IPv6 egress traffic, matching the IPv4 capability introduced in Cilium 1.19. ([cilium/cilium#44234](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44234), @Andreagit97)
    * 🌐 **Select the Entire Cluster Mesh**: The new `cluster-mesh` policy entity selects every endpoint across a mesh, making cross-cluster security policies easier to express. ([cilium/cilium#46813](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46813), @squeed)
    * ☁️ **Standardize AWS VPC Group Policies**: Policies that reference AWS VPC groups are now transformed into `CiliumCIDRGroup` resources, bringing external IP groups into the standard Cilium policy model. ([cilium/cilium#44704](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44704), @squeed)
    * 🛂 **Per-Pod Source IP Verification Control**: Trusted workloads that need to send traffic with non-local source addresses can disable source IP verification through a pod annotation, guarded by a namespace-level opt-in. ([cilium/cilium#43505](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43505), @zbb88888)


* ⚙️ **Day 2 Operations and Observability**
    * 🔧 **Detect Configuration Drift**: Cilium can expose how many ConfigMap settings an agent has not yet applied, making it easier to identify when a restart is required after a configuration change. ([cilium/cilium#44703](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44703), @PhilipSchmid)
    * ⏱️ **Understand Agent Start-Up Time**: New Hive lifecycle and Kubernetes resource-sync metrics show how long individual resources and components take to initialize. ([cilium/cilium#44802](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44802), [cilium/cilium#44639](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44639), @ILL1A)
    * 🛰️ **Correlate More Hubble Verdicts with Policies**: Hubble can now identify the policy responsible for audit verdicts. ([cilium/cilium#45373](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45373), @Rajneesh180)
    * 📊 **Standalone DNS Proxy Metrics**: The Standalone DNS Proxy now exports DNS metrics back through Cilium, improving visibility when DNS policy processing runs outside the agent. ([cilium/cilium#45222](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45222), [cilium/cilium#44601](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44601), @vipul-21)


* 🌅 **Performance and Scale**
    * 💾 **Aggregated Load-Balancer State**: Cilium's internal backend representation has been flattened to efficiently support thousands of Services that share the same backends. ([cilium/cilium#44511](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44511), @joamaki)
    * 📡 **More Efficient Envoy Updates**: New ADS and Delta xDS modes provide consistent or incremental delivery of Envoy resources, reducing CPU usage and policy update latency. ([cilium/cilium#43887](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43887), @nezdolik; [cilium/cilium#45288](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45288), @jrajahalme)
    * 🗂️ **Optimized BPF Policy Map Encoding**: Semantic wildcard identities for remote-node and world reduce BPF policy-map pressure, particularly in larger clusters. ([cilium/cilium#46438](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46438), @squeed)
    * 📦 **Smaller CNI Binary**: The `cilium-cni` binary has been reduced from roughly 77 MB to 16 MB, shrinking both the Cilium image and its footprint on every node. ([cilium/cilium#45845](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45845), @giorio94)
    * 🛠️ **Updated Dependencies and Foundations**: Cilium 1.20 updates to Kubernetes v1.36, Envoy v1.37.x, Gateway API v1.6.1, GoBGP v4.6.1 and MCS API v0.5.2. Runtime and builder images now use Ubuntu 26.04, and the default CNI configuration version moves from 0.3.1 to 1.0.0. ([cilium/cilium#45499](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45499), [cilium/cilium#47215](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/47215), @HadrienPatte; [cilium/cilium#45851](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45851), @sayboras; [cilium/cilium#47274](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/47274), @arybolovlev; [cilium/cilium#45952](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45952), @rastislavs; [cilium/cilium#47166](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/47166), @MrFreezeex; [cilium/cilium#46971](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46971), @gandro)


* 🏠 **Community**
    * ❤️ **Production Case Studies**: Many end-users have told their stories running Cilium in production. Read and watch more from: [Asana](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mxjiSCnrb3c), [Etraveli](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KWS-NaZd62M&list=PLDg_GiBbAx-mSQHa1y9Z9sjBYUmG2FBCZ&index=7), [Michelin](https://www.cncf.io/case-studies/michelin-2/), [OpenAI](https://isovalent.com/blog/post/openai-isovalent-networking-kubernetes-case-study/), [Suse](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bgCg1tS72ME&list=PLDg_GiBbAx-mSQHa1y9Z9sjBYUmG2FBCZ&index=8), [Telefónica's acens](https://blogs.cisco.com/sp/telefonicas-acens-and-cisco-driving-the-next-generation-of-cloud-native-services-with-isovalent), and [Zynga](https://www.cncf.io/case-studies/zynga/). If your company wants to submit their case studies let us know. We would love to hear your feedback!
    * 🇳🇱 **Amsterdam Events**: The community gathered at [CiliumCon](https://events.linuxfoundation.org/kubecon-cloudnativecon-europe/co-located-events/ciliumcon/) and [Cilium Developer Summit](https://github.com/cilium/dev-summits/tree/main/2026-EU) in Amsterdam. [Watch the talks](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLDg_GiBbAx-mSQHa1y9Z9sjBYUmG2FBCZ) from CiliumCon.
    * 🇺🇸 **Salt Lake City Events**: Meet us at the upcoming [CiliumCon](https://events.linuxfoundation.org/kubecon-cloudnativecon-north-america/co-located-events/ciliumcon/) and Cilium Developer Summit at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America in Salt Lake City, November 9-12.
    * 🤖 **Generative AI Policy**: The Cilium community adopted a [Generative AI Policy](https://github.com/cilium/community/blob/main/AI-POLICY.md) that encourages community members to connect and communicate with one another without the use of AI, while recognizing that different people work best with their own tools of choice.
    * 📚 **Cilium Books**: Two new books landed for readers at every level — _[Cilium: Up and Running](https://isovalent.com/books/cilium-up-and-running/)_ (O'Reilly), a practitioner's deep dive and _[Buzzing Beyond Clouds: The Illustrated Children's Guide to Cilium](https://isovalent.com/books/children-guide-to-cilium/)_, the follow-up to the eBPF children's guide.

❤️ **Thank You**: Cilium 1.20 was made possible by contributors, reviewers and maintainers from across the community, including engineers from Datadog, Google, Microsoft and many other organizations.

To keep up to date with all the latest Cilium releases, join #release 🎉

upcoming.title: 1.21.0-pre.0
upcoming.description:
Summary of Changes
------------------

**Major Changes:**
* Envoy resources (e.g., Listeners, Network Policies, etc.) can now be synchronized with Envoy incrementally, reducing CPU load and policy update latency. This is enabled by the new agent option value `--envoy-xds-mode=delta-split`. Corresponding Helm value is `envoy.xdsMode=delta-split`. (cilium/cilium#45288, @jrajahalme)
* network driver: add agent side baseline driver and dummy device manager (cilium/cilium#47254, @bersoare)

**Minor Changes:**
* build: Update iptables from 1.8.8 to 1.8.11 (cilium/cilium#47623, @HadrienPatte)
* clustermesh: no longer restart pods when changing remote clustermesh-apiserver IPs statically defined (without a DNS name) (cilium/cilium#47190, @MrFreezeex)
* CT map adaptive GC interval calculation improvements (cilium/cilium#46796, @fristonio)
* Deprecate WireGuard Node Encryption (cilium/cilium#47219, @pchaigno)
* envoy: demote stale ADS endpoint warning (cilium/cilium#47148, @nezdolik)

signals.title: Communication from world with lower MTU is failing to LoadBalancer services
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [X] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.16.0 and lower than v1.17.0 ### What happened? I'm having troubles talking onto LoadBalancer services from outside "world" when user is on lower MTU than cluster's. It seems like ICMP "fragmentation needed" is not delivered to the pod. Instead it loops on k8s host until its TTL exceedes. I've seen lots of issues around this but it LOOKS like it SHOULD (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/12854 https://github.com/industrialdiscipline/cilium/commit/07edf550cab7f865ef83522061256183a803109e) be solved. Unfortunately not for me. Interesting is I can't see any drops of ICMP using cilium monitor. TBH I'm pretty new to cilium so I'm a little confused how to debug this any further. So I've tried to use tcpdump all around and draw a scheme of what I think is happening where red line is what is **wrong** and dotted lines are what SHOULD happen. I hope it makes sense. Cilium is installed with helm using these values: ### How can we reproduce the issue? * Install cilium with helm using this values: ``` bpf: hostLegacyRouting: false masquerade: true cluster: name: <CUT> cni: customConf: false uninstall: false ipam: mode: cluster-pool operator: clusterPoolIPv4PodCIDRList: - 10.98.0.0/16 clusterPoolIPv6PodCIDRList: - fd11:1111:1111::/112 operator: replicas: 1 unmanagedPodWatcher: restart: true policyEnforcementMode: default routingMode: tunnel tunnelProtocol: vxlan kubeProxyReplacement: true k8sServiceHost: <CUT> k8sServicePort: 6443 hubble: relay: enabled: false ui: <CUT> ipv4: enabled: true ipv6: enabled: true pmtuDiscovery: enabled: true fragmentTracking: true ``` * create a ciliumloadbalancerippools * create a service of type LoadBalancer, let it allocate IP * Have a machine with lower MTU somewhere else. signals.title: bpf: migrate non-branching config macros to runtime configuration
signals.text: The current step in the clang-freedom (pre-compiled eBPF programs) journey is to start transitioning compile time configuration to load-time (runtime) configuration. The necessary agent and loader infrastructure has been merged. Runtime configuration can be defined with [`DECLARE_CONFIG` and `NODE_CONFIG`](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/bpf/lib/static_data.h). See [Configuring the Datapath](https://docs.cilium.io/en/latest/contributing/development/datapath_config) in the Cilium Developer docs for guidelines and principles. ~~This issue specifically tracks variables which do not influence control flow by enabling or disabling certain code paths. Variables used in `#ifdef`/`#if` and `if(is_defined(...))` will be converted in 1.19 since dead code elimination only really landed in Linux 5.5, and Cilium 1.18 targets Linux 5.4 which will go EOL at the end of 2025.~~ 1.19 targets Linux 5.10. We can migrate branching macros, too. Additionally, https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/41628 shipped in 1.19 which added dead code detection in the agent to avoid loading unused maps and tail calls. Branching macros can now safely be ported. This issue is for migrating `node_config.h` and `WriteNodeConfig` entries to `config.Node`, as well as some leftover per-object configs in `ep_config.h`. Through this issue, we can coordinate work and keep an overview. If you want to work on a particular (set of) variable(s), drop a comment and we'll spin out an issue or assign you to a list item. The list may change over time and may grow as we find more work in this category. When migrating variables, do a quick search through [Paul's macro documentation](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/15379#issuecomment-897441189) for a good docstring to use in `DECLARE_CONFIG`. - [ep_config.h](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/bpf/ep_config.h) - [x] HOST_EP_ID - [x] DIRECT_ROUTING_DEV_IFINDEX - [node_config.h](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/bpf/node_config.h) - [x] CLUSTER_ID - [x] CILIUM_*_IFINDEX, CILIUM_*_MAC (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43474) - [x] TUNNEL_PORT, TUNNEL_PROTOCOL (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43520) - [x] KERNEL_HZ, ENABLE_JIFFIES (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43112) - [x] L2_ANNOUNCEMENTS(_MAX_LIVENESS) (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/42587) - [x] EPHEMERAL_MIN (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43564) - [x] IS_L3_DEV, NATIVE_DEV_MAC_BY_IFINDEX (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/39116 & https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43680) - [x] CLUSTER_ID_MAX (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/42478) - [x] IDENTITY_{LEN,MAX} (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43507) - [x] VTEP_MASK (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43112) - [x] NODEPORT_PORT_* (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43680) - [x] IPV4_LOOPBACK (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/38818) - [x] NAT_46X64_PREFIX (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43799) - [x] CIDR_IDENTITY_RANGE_{START,END} (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44223) - [x] HASH_INIT{4,6}_SEED (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44190) - [x] EVENTS_MAP_* (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44795) - [ ] VLAN_FILTER (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/38721) - [x] Reserved security IDs (HOST_ID, WORLD_ID, ect.) signals.title: CFP: Make fixed (reserved/well known) identities granular per cluster for Cluster Mesh
signals.text: ## Cilium Feature Proposal **Is your proposed feature related to a problem?** Currently, all Cilium identities with a fixed numeric identity are in the 0-256 range **regardless of their cluster**. This mostly means the reserved identities, but also the well-known ones (well-known identities are disabled by default and do not seem to have a lot of usage though). As a result, we essentially accept CiliumEndpoint(Slice) objects from remote clusters with identities in the 0-256 range and users can not have per cluster granularity. The most problematic consequence of this is for the ingress identity/entity. A NetworkPolicy accepting traffic from ingress necessarily accepts traffic from all connected clusters. This means that a user in a connected cluster who can create ingress/Gateway API resources (or anything else that makes traffic act as the ingress identity) could theoretically circumvent some network policies if they allow traffic from the ingress identity. **Describe the feature you'd like** Change all reserved/well-known identities to use each cluster identity range. Like cluster ID 0, we would use the first 256 IDs from each cluster range for those reserved/well-known identities. As the ingress identity seems the main concern among all the reserved / well known identity we could potentially restrict the scope of this change to only the ingress identity. This approach was mostly suggested by @squeed and @joestringer during the community meeting on the 11th of March (and I then took some time to open this mostly because of KubeCon 😅). **Notify relevant community channels** - @cilium/sig-policy - @cilium/sig-clustermesh **(Optional) Describe your proposed solution** Here are a few work streams/problems that we would need to solve (this is mostly me filing the blanks and discovering the future issues that we might have but it is potentially not exhaustive): 1) ID reservation We currently reserve the first 256 IDs only for cluster 0 -> https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/50d46815862602a849c2a060f6f629820a0bfa27/pkg/identity/numericidentity.go#L355 :(. What we could potentially do here is start changing the allocation code so that it never hands out new identities in that range (the linked function appears to be used for validation too, so we would need to introduce a new function and change specifically the allocation logic). In the long run, this should help empty that range. Depending on how confident we are with this part of the change, we could potentially backport it to all/some stable versions to increase the chance that those IDs would be mostly empty by the time users upgrade on a version where we actually start using those. When we start to actually use those IDs, we could have a preflight check that fails if there are still allocated IDs, and some command/instructions to spot the remaining identities that should be rotated. For instance, we could have some script/command that helps trace back the identity to the top-most resource (like Deployment/sts/ds/...) which should then be rolled out with new labels in its pods. A rollout like this should be safe netpol wise, and most Kubernetes users should be accustomed to such rollouts for Kubernetes version upgrades among other things. Note that this would only affect cluster with an ID different than 0. 2) Start using the new identity numeric IDs We should start to actually make the cluster ID influence the numeric ID of all reserved / well-known identities (or only the ingress identity if we restrict the scope to this only) and include the cluster label in the identity labels for the reserved identities. Only the identity should change, and probably not the underlying selector behind the entities, as we probably do not want to break existing network policies that select all clusters (we might (?) discuss doing this later on, but it is probably better not to mix that topic right now). Besides that, I do not really know how much of this can be done in a non-disruptive way (and whether it is actually possible to do it in a non-disruptive way at all). For instance, for the ingress identity, it might be possible to make it essentially like a pod rollout and keep both identities while starting to use the new one "gracefully" (since the envoy pod is separated from the cilium-agent it might be an actual pod rollout, but this might not work in practice ~). 3) Make remote clusters understand those new identities Currently, there is no actual CiliumIdentity created for those reserved/well-known identities and since it is currently the same identity for every cluster it just "works". But if we start using per-cluster identities for those, the remote cluster should actually know about them. In order to solve that, we could make each cluster create its own CiliumIdentity objects (in k8s or kvstore) for reserved/well-known identities. Alternatively, we could allocate the identities locally for each connected cluster, but this would make forward compatibility very hard when we start using those per-cluster reserved numeric identities and even anytime we introduce new identities. So this does not seem viable. Another choice could be to inject "fake" identities at the clustermesh-apiserver level because we only read this data from remote clusters, but unfortunately this does not work when kvstore is used because in that case kvstore is read from both the local cluster and remote clusters :(. So if we were to do this we would still need to actually create the CiliumIdentity objects in kvstore mode... 4) Cluster Mesh cleanups Once we have done everything above, we could probably start to not accept identities/endpoints in the 0-256 range from clusters which are not cluster 0. This should probably be done in a minor release after everything above was released to make version upgrades smooth (note that Cluster Mesh supports only 1 minor version skew). ----- This is mostly outside my main area of expertise, so I would gladly help with adjacent things if needed (like problems 1 and 4 here), but otherwise I am looking for someone who knows this a little better than me for the main policy changes 😅 🙏.

signals.title: Migrate `pkg/node/types.Node` to `netip`
signals.text: ### Is your proposed feature related to a problem? This issue is a subissue of the larger netip migration (#24246). The scope is migrating [`pkg/node/types.Node`](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/080b189e9f7b97af40b8e74632a15f8551539b9a/pkg/node/types/node.go#L39)'s fields from `net.IP` and `*cidr.CIDR` to their [netip](https://pkg.go.dev/net/netip) equivalents. ## The problem: `Node` is a kvstore wire contract `Node` implements `store.Key` and is serialized to the kvstore with `json.Marshal` ([`Node.Marshal`](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/080b189e9f7b97af40b8e74632a15f8551539b9a/pkg/node/types/node.go#L476-L479)), then shared across independently-upgraded agents and, via kvstoremesh, across clustermesh clusters. Its JSON is therefore a cross-version, cross-cluster wire contract, and the fields have no `json` tags: they serialize under their Go names. The problem is specific to the `*cidr.CIDR` fields. `cidr.CIDR` embeds `*net.IPNet` and neither type defines any JSON marshaler, so `net.IPNet` falls back to default struct marshaling of its exported fields and because `net.IPMask` is a `[]byte` with no `MarshalText`, the mask is base64-encoded. In practice, this means a `*cidr.CIDR` for `10.244.1.0/24` currently serializes to JSON as `{"IP":"10.244.1.0","Mask":"////AA=="}` while the equivalent `netip.Prefix` would serialize to the `"10.244.1.0/24"` JSON string because `netip.Prefix` implements [`MarshalText`](https://pkg.go.dev/net/netip#Prefix.MarshalText) which `json.Marshal` falls back to. A naive migration replacing the `*cidr.CIDR` with `netip.Prefix` would cause issues during upgrade as their JSON serialized formats are not compatible. A new node emitting `"10.244.1.0/24"` could not be deserialized by an old agent expecting the `{"IP":...,"Mask":...}` form and vice-versa. Note: the good news is that the `net.IP` fields do not have this issue as this type does implement [`MarshalText`](https://pkg.go.dev/net#IP.MarshalText) and so they are fully compatible with `netip.Addr`: * net.IP -> `"10.0.0.5"` * netip.Addr -> `"10.0.0.5"` * nil net.IP -> `""` * zero netip.Addr -> `""` Example: ``` $ kubectl exec cilium-agent-9vxhn -c cilium-agent -- cilium-dbg kvstore get cilium/state/nodes/v1/CLUSTER_NAME/NODE_NAME Creating etcd client Connecting to etcd server... New lease successfully acquired Starting watcher Successfully listed keys before starting watcher Initial etcd connection established Starting to watch prefix cilium/state/nodes/v1/CLUSTER_NAME/NODE_NAME => {"Name":"NODE_NAME","Cluster":"CLUSTER_NAME","IPAddresses":[{"Type":"InternalIP","IP":"10.16.60.112"},{"Type":"CiliumInternalIP","IP":"10.19.193.137"}],"IPv4AllocCIDR":{"IP":"10.19.193.128","Mask":"////8A=="},"IPv4SecondaryAllocCIDRs":null,"IPv6AllocCIDR":null,"IPv6SecondaryAllocCIDRs":null,"IPv4HealthIP":"","IPv6HealthIP":"","IPv4IngressIP":"","IPv6IngressIP":"","ClusterID":1,"Source":"local","EncryptionKey":0,"Labels":{"beta.kubernetes.io/arch":"amd64","beta.kubernetes.io/instance-type":"n2d-standard-8","beta.kubernetes.io/os":"linux","disk-type.gke.io/hyperdisk-throughput":"true","disk-type.gke.io/pd-balanced":"true","disk-type.gke.io/pd-extreme":"true","disk-type.gke.io/pd-ssd":"true","disk-type.gke.io/pd-standard":"true","failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/region":"europe-west3","failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone":"europe-west3-c","kubernetes.io/arch":"amd64","kubernetes.io/hostname":"NODE_NAME","kubernetes.io/os":"linux","node.kubernetes.io/instance-type":"n2d-standard-8","topology.gke.io/zone":"europe-west3-c","topology.kubernetes.io/region":"europe-west3","topology.kubernetes.io/zone":"europe-west3-c"},"Annotations":{},"NodeIdentity":1,"WireguardPubKey":"","BootID":"84119f79-c8d9-455a-9a12-d216cb98fbd3"} ``` Or pretty-printed: ```json { "Name": "NODE_NAME", "Cluster": "CLUSTER_NAME", "IPAddresses": [ { "Type": "InternalIP", "IP": "10.16.60.112" }, { "Type": "CiliumInternalIP", "IP": "10.19.193.137" } ], "IPv4AllocCIDR": { "IP": "10.19.193.128", "Mask": "////8A==" }, "IPv4SecondaryAllocCIDRs": null, "IPv6AllocCIDR": null, "IPv6SecondaryAllocCIDRs": null, "IPv4HealthIP": "", "IPv6HealthIP": "", "IPv4IngressIP": "", "IPv6IngressIP": "", "ClusterID": 1, "Source": "local", "EncryptionKey": 0, "Labels": { "beta.kubernetes.io/arch": "amd64", "beta.kubernetes.io/instance-type": "n2d-standard-8", "beta.kubernetes.io/os": "linux", "disk-type.gke.io/hyperdisk-throughput": "true", "disk-type.gke.io/pd-balanced": "true", "disk-type.gke.io/pd-extreme": "true", "disk-type.gke.io/pd-ssd": "true", "disk-type.gke.io/pd-standard": "true", "failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/region": "europe-west3", "failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone": "europe-west3-c", "kubernetes.io/arch": "amd64", "kubernetes.io/hostname": "NODE_NAME", "kubernetes.io/os": "linux", "node.kubernetes.io/instance-type": "n2d-standard-8", "topology.gke.io/zone": "europe-west3-c", "topology.kubernetes.io/region": "europe-west3", "topology.kubernetes.io/zone": "europe-west3-c" }, "Annotations": {}, "NodeIdentity": 1, "WireguardPubKey": "", "BootID": "84119f79-c8d9-455a-9a12-d216cb98fbd3" } ``` The above node example comes from a cluster using [kubernetes IPAM mode](https://docs.cilium.io/en/stable/network/concepts/ipam/kubernetes/) in IPv4-only mode. We can confirm that because `IPv4AllocCIDR` is set and `IPv6AllocCIDR` isn't. We can also observe how those two `*cidr.CIDR` each get serialized: `IPv4AllocCIDR` gets the IP/Mask fields described above (`"IP":"10.19.193.128","Mask":"////8A=="}`) while `IPv6AllocCIDR` is the literal `null` since `Node` fields don't set either [`omitempty`](https://pkg.go.dev/encoding/json#Marshal) or [`omitzero`](https://pkg.go.dev/encoding/json#Marshal) so they all always get serialized, even if `nil`. ### Describe the feature you'd like ## Proposed approach: transitional wrapper with dual-format marshaling The proposed solution is to introduce a transitional field type (e.g. `pkg/node/types.Prefix`) that embeds the end-state `ip.Prefix` (so we converge on the canonical wrapper and don't migrate twice) but with custom JSON Marshal/Unmarshal methods: * `MarshalJSON` keeps emitting the legacy `{"IP","Mask"}` object (byte-exact), and `null` for an unset value (matching a nil `*cidr.CIDR`). * `UnmarshalJSON` accepts both the (current) legacy object and the target string form, plus `null`. ### Rollout lifecycle 1. Release N (1.21): read both formats, write legacy. Old peers keep working. 2. Release N+1 (1.22): once all supported versions can read both, flip `MarshalJSON` to write the string form. 3. Release N+2 (1.23): drop the wrapper, the fields become plain `ip.Prefix`, whose inherited `MarshalText` already emits the string form. ### Notify relevant community channels _No response_ ### (Optional) Describe your proposed solution _No response_

signals.title: Per-packet service LB: embedded packet inside ICMP Fragmentation Needed is not reverse-translated, breaking PMTUD for ClusterIP flows
signals.text: ## Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues Closest matches found: #39773 (host firewall / DNAT reply misrouting in tunnel mode) and #46993 (PMTU handling for L4 services, DSR/Maglev) — neither describes this: the outer header of an ICMP error is reverse-translated for a ClusterIP flow while the embedded original packet is not. ## What happened? For pod→ClusterIP traffic handled by the per-packet service load balancer (socket LB disabled), when a hop behind the backend pod returns **ICMP type 3 code 4 (Fragmentation Needed)**, Cilium reverse-translates the **outer** IP header of the ICMP error (source becomes the ClusterIP), but the **embedded original packet inside the ICMP payload keeps the post-DNAT tuple** (backend pod IP / target port instead of ClusterIP / service port). The client kernel matches ICMP errors to sockets by the embedded tuple. The socket is connected to `ClusterIP:port`, the embedded packet says `podIP:targetPort`, so the error is discarded. Path MTU discovery never happens: the client retransmits the same oversized DF segment until the connection times out. Any TCP flow whose segments exceed the bottleneck MTU black-holes; small requests work, which makes this very confusing to diagnose (it presents as "TLS handshakes and SSH hang through ClusterIP, everything works via pod IP"). tcpdump on the client pod (socket connected to ClusterIP `10.100.170.252:8080`, backend pod `10.244.27.179`): ``` IP 10.100.170.252 > 10.244.29.246: ICMP 10.244.27.179 unreachable - need to frag (mtu 800), length 556 IP 10.244.29.246.34672 > 10.244.27.179.8080: Flags [P.], ... length 1555 POST / HTTP/1.1 Host: 10.100.170.252:8080 ``` Outer source is the ClusterIP (translated), the embedded destination is still the pod IP (not translated). The same request sent directly to the pod IP receives an identical ICMP whose embedded tuple matches the socket, the kernel lowers the path MTU, retransmits smaller segments and the request completes in ~2 ms. Via the ClusterIP the client retransmits the full-size segment 7 times and times out. Expected behavior: the embedded packet should be reverse-translated together with the outer header (destination rewritten back to `ClusterIP:servicePort`), which is what netfilter's SNAT/DNAT does for ICMP errors (RFC 5508 §4.2 semantics). Datapath config where this was hit: `routing-mode=tunnel`, `tunnel-protocol=vxlan`, `kube-proxy-replacement=true`, `bpf-lb-sock=false` (per-packet service translation), `enable-bpf-masquerade` unset (iptables masquerade), host firewall enabled. Real-world trigger was a Tailscale egress proxy pod (tun MTU 1280) fronted by a ClusterIP Service, but the repro below is self-contained. ## How can we reproduce the issue? Backend pod that forwards into a low-MTU link inside its own netns (stand-in for any VPN/tunnel proxy pod): ```bash kubectl run repro-backend --image=nicolaka/netshoot --restart=Never \ --overrides='{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"repro-backend","image":"nicolaka/netshoot","command":["sleep","1800"],"securityContext":{"privileged":true}}]}}' kubectl exec repro-backend -- bash -c ' ip netns add inner ip link add veth0 type veth peer name veth1 ip link set veth1 netns inner ip addr add 192.168.99.1/30 dev veth0 ip link set veth0 mtu 800 up ip netns exec inner ip addr add 192.168.99.2/30 dev veth1 ip netns exec inner ip link set veth1 mtu 1500 up ip netns exec inner ip link set lo up ip netns exec inner ip route add default via 192.168.99.1 sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -p tcp --dport 8080 -j DNAT --to-destination 192.168.99.2:8080 ip netns exec inner sh -c "cd /tmp && nohup python3 -m http.server 8080 >/dev/null 2>&1 &"' kubectl expose pod repro-backend --name repro-svc --port 8080 ``` Client pod **on a different node** (so the flow crosses the tunnel): ```bash kubectl run repro-client --image=nicolaka/netshoot --restart=Never --command -- sleep 1800 kubectl exec repro-client -- bash -c ' head -c 1400 /dev/zero | tr "\0" "A" > /tmp/big tcpdump -nn -v -i eth0 icmp & sleep 2 curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "via ClusterIP: %{http_code} %{time_total}s\n" -m 8 -X POST --data-binary @/tmp/big http://<CLUSTER_IP>:8080/ || true curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "via pod IP: %{http_code} %{time_total}s\n" -m 8 -X POST --data-binary @/tmp/big http://<POD_IP>:8080/ || true' ``` Result: - via ClusterIP: `000 8.0s` (timeout) — ICMP arrives with outer src = ClusterIP but embedded dst = pod IP, client keeps retransmitting the 1450-byte segment; - via pod IP: `501 0.002s` (instant; 501 is just python http.server rejecting POST) — same ICMP, embedded tuple matches the socket, PMTUD works. ## Cilium Version ``` Client: 1.17.3 3993bd06 2025-04-09T16:59:44+00:00 go version go1.23.8 linux/amd64 Daemon: 1.17.3 3993bd06 2025-04-09T16:59:44+00:00 go version go1.23.8 linux/amd64 ``` ## Kernel Version ``` Linux 6.8.0-90-generic x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS) ``` ## Kubernetes Version ``` v1.31.1 (kubeadm) ``` ## Regression Unknown — first noticed on 1.17.3; we have no data from earlier versions. ## Sysdump Not attached (production cluster); can provide targeted `cilium-dbg monitor` captures or specific map dumps on request. ## Relevant log output `cilium-dbg monitor -vv` on the client node during a stalled TLS handshake through a ClusterIP (backend is a proxy pod with tun MTU 1280; service `10.105.148.60:443` → `10.244.2.99:10162`): ```shell Policy verdict log: ... 10.244.29.231:59052 -> 10.244.2.99:10162 tcp SYN # post-DNAT -- to-endpoint: SYN/ACK SrcIP=10.105.148.60 -> 10.244.29.231 # outer rev-DNAT OK -- to-overlay: 1594-byte DF (TLS ClientHello) 10.244.29.231 -> 10.244.2.99 -- to-endpoint: ICMPv4 DestinationUnreachable(FragmentationNeeded) mtu=1280 SrcIP=10.105.148.60 -> 10.244.29.231, state related # outer translated ... client retransmits the same 1594-byte segment, same ICMP repeats, connection stalls until the peer closes (~10 s) ``` No drop events are emitted (`cilium-dbg monitor -t drop` stays silent for these flows) — nothing is dropped by the datapath, the PMTU signal is just unusable by the client. ## Anything else? - Works: same flow addressed to the backend **pod IP** (PMTUD functions normally). - Workaround we deployed: TCP MSS clamping (`iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1240`) inside the proxy pods, so no oversized segments are ever produced and the broken ICMP path is never needed. - `bpf-lb-sock=true` should also avoid it (socket tuple would match the embedded packet), but that is a cluster-wide datapath change. - Possibly related: #39773, #46993. ## Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the Users doc ## Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: CFP: First Class MCS Support for GAMMA Routes
signals.text: ### Is your proposed feature related to a problem? Right now a MCS cannot be reference via a GAMMA route directly, instead its derived, real matching service must be referenced as a backend. This works fine in practice, but there is no typed contract mapping Service Import <-> derived hash so you have to repeat the algorithm to hash the import. ### Describe the feature you'd like I would like to be able to use the kind ServiceImport inside a GAMMA route Instead of doing: `parentRefs: - kind: Service group: "" name: derived-1a2b3c4d5e port: 8080` I'd like to be able to do: `parentRefs: - kind: ServiceImport group: multicluster.x-k8s.io name: my-svc port: 8080` ### Notify relevant community channels _No response_ ### (Optional) Describe your proposed solution I'd like to work on this issue!

signals.title: Gateway API Envoy cannot connect to backend pod on the same node while remote-node backend works
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.19.6 and lower than v1.20.0 ### What happened? I am using Cilium Gateway API with an external Envoy DaemonSet and a hostNetwork Gateway listener. The Gateway is restricted to one node (`node B`) using: ```yaml gatewayAPI: enabled: true hostNetwork: enabled: true nodes: matchLabels: gateway-node: "true" ``` The backend Service has two healthy pod endpoints: 10.244.4.70:5556 on the same node as the Gateway/Envoy (node B) 10.244.0.92:5556 on another node (node A) Requests through the Gateway intermittently return HTTP 503: ``` upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. reset reason: connection timeout ``` Envoy's cluster statistics show that the remote-node backend works consistently, while the same-node backend cannot establish a TCP connection: ``` 10.244.0.92:5556 (remote node) cx_connect_fail: 0 rq_success: >0 10.244.4.70:5556 (same node) cx_connect_fail: increasing rq_success: 0 ``` Envoy EDS contains both endpoints and marks both as healthy. signals.title: Corrupted IP address in OLD_CILIUM_POST_nat rule reconciliation
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.19.6 and lower than v1.20.0 ### What happened? What happened? During iptables full reconciliation, cilium-agent fails to remove a stale rule from the OLD_CILIUM_POST_nat backup chain because the destination CIDR it's trying to delete does not match any rule actually present on the host. The destination IP in the failing delete command is not a real IP — it's the raw ASCII bytes of an unrelated string, reinterpreted as a dotted-decimal IPv4 address. Observed on Cilium 1.19.5: ``` time=2026-08-13T14:46:32.891072206Z level=error msg="iptables rules full reconciliation failed, will retry another one later" module=agent.datapath.iptables error="failed to remove old backup rules: unable to run 'iptables -t nat -D OLD_CILIUM_POST_nat -s 10.0.0.0/24 -d 101.110.115.57/16 -o ens9f0 -m comment --comment cilium snat pod to OOB mgmt network -j SNAT --to-source 192.168.2.61' iptables command: exit status 1 stderr=\"iptables: Bad rule (does a matching rule exist in that chain?).\\n\"" ``` Decoding 101.110.115.57 as ASCII bytes: ``` 101 = 'e' 110 = 'n' 115 = 's' 57 = '9' ``` → spells ens9, the first four characters of the egress interface name ens9f0 used later in the same rule (-o ens9f0). The actual rule present on the host in that chain is: ``` -A OLD_CILIUM_POST_nat -s 10.0.0.0/24 -d 192.168.0.0/16 -o ens9f0 -m comment --comment "cilium snat pod to OOB mgmt network" -j SNAT --to-source 192.168.2.61 ``` i.e. the real destination is 192.168.0.0/16, not 101.110.115.57/16. Cilium is regenerating the "old" rule it intends to delete with a corrupted destination address, so the iptables -D never matches, and full reconciliation fails and retries indefinitely. Similar issue : https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/33465 ### How can we reproduce the issue? 1. Installed Openshift with Isovalent operator 2. Updated the daemonset and other configs to picks up the open source 1.19.5 version 3. On start up of cilium pods , this issue is observed ### Cilium Version Open source version 1.19.5 running on Openshift 4.20 ### Kernel Version [core@master02 ~]$ cat /etc/os-release NAME="Red Hat signals.title: clustermesh: security hardening
signals.text: The security posture of Cluster Mesh is currently roughly described as "meshed clusters are trusted" and does provide substantial protection against an adversarial remote cluster. This issue tracks the improvement of both the posture and its documentation. Known attacks that a connected cluster may perform include: - Workload or reserved-identity impersonation from a remote cluster - Cross-cluster load-balancing being manipulated to blackhole or divert service traffic to malicious or unintended destinations The following potential attacks would need some investigation: - DOS attack trying to exhaust the QPS of a local kvstoremesh - Unexpected/malformed keys/values in etcd producing unexpected result There may also be other type of attacks possible

signals.title: host-firewall-egress-to-fqdns connectivity test fails on RHEL8.10
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.20.0 and lower than v1.21.0 ### What happened? host-firewall-egress-to-fqdns consistently fails in the kube-proxy-1 configuration (using RHEL8.10 kernel) in both ipv4 and ipv6 flavors, although it appears to succeed in all other configurations and cases it runs in (on newer kernels). It is unclear why this happens. Other L7 tests (to-fqdns, client-egress-l7, client-egress-l7-named-port, client-egress-tls-cni) using pod-to-world scenarios are also disabled on RHEL kernels, see commit message in https://github.com/cilium/cilium/commit/b1d70aace8944805dd634ae80b66a4b2be18016c. Possibly the reason this test fails on RHEL is related to that. Also note that this test, as well as the other L7 tests disabled on RHEL, use fake external targets provisioned in Docker. CI runs in which this failure has occurred are listed [here](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/47921#issuecomment-5282481311). The test is currently disabled on RHEL kernels to make scheduled CI runs usable. This issue tracks the underlying bug. ### How can we reproduce the issue? Re-enable the host-firewall-egress-to-fqdns connectivity test on RHEL and run it in the kube-proxy-1 configuration: ``` kernel: 'rhel8.10' kube-proxy: 'iptables' kpr: 'false' tunnel: 'vxlan' host-fw: 'true' ``` ### Cilium Version main branch ### Kernel Version lvh-image-kind_rhel8.10-20260803.013611_amd64 ### Kubernetes Version 1.36.0 ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump _No response_ ### Relevant log output ```shell Action [host-firewall-egress-to-fqdns/host-to-world:http-to-fake.external.service.cilium-0: cilium-test-1/host-netns-8h6h4 (172.20.0.4) -> fake.external.service.cilium-http (fake.external.service.cilium:80)] ❌ command "curl --silent --fail --show-error --connect-timeout 2 --max-time 10 -4 -w %{local_ip}:%{local_port} -> %{remote_ip}:%{remote_port} = %{response_code}\n --output /dev/null [http://fake.external.service.cilium:80](http://fake.external.service.cilium/)" failed: command failed (pod=cilium-test-1/host-netns-8h6h4, container=host-netns): command terminated with exit code 28 ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? signals.title: The working (hostNetwork) per-Ingress configs show up properly wired — Selected: true, with a real listener. kube-system/cilium-ingress — the shared LoadBalancer Service — has no entry in this table at all.
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.20.0 and lower than v1.21.0 ### What happened? When the shared Ingress controller is configured with ingressController.hostNetwork.enabled: false and ingressController.service.type: LoadBalancer (instead of the hostNetwork exposure model), the operator creates the shared cilium-ingress LoadBalancer Service and it correctly receives an IP from CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool (and, separately, gets BGP-advertised via CiliumBGPAdvertisement — that part works). However, no CiliumEnvoyConfig is ever generated for the shared kube-system/cilium-ingress Service, so there is no listener and no redirect target behind it. The Service's eBPF frontend ends up with zero backends and zero RedirectTo, and any TCP connection to the LoadBalancer IP gets an immediate "connection refused." ### How can we reproduce the issue? Verified via the newer cilium-dbg shell db/show ciliumenvoyconfigs statedb command: Name Selected Services BackendServices Listeners llm-serving/cilium-ingress-llm-serving-sglang-ingress true llm-serving/cilium-ingress-sglang-ingress llm-serving/sglang-service llm-serving/cilium-ingress-llm-serving-sglang-ingress/listener:8080 llm-serving/cilium-ingress-llm-serving-vllm-ingress true llm-serving/cilium-ingress-vllm-ingress llm-serving/vllm-service llm-serving/cilium-ingress-llm-serving-vllm-ingress/listener:8080 Note there is no entry at all for kube-system/cilium-ingress (the shared LB service), while the individual per-Ingress hostNetwork-backed configs (cilium-ingress-llm-serving-*-ingress, still present from before the config change) show up correctly with Selected: true and a real listener. cilium-dbg shell db/show frontends confirms the shared service's frontends are empty end-to-end: Address Type ServiceName PortName Backends RedirectTo Status 0.0.0.0:32236/TCP NodePort kube-system/cilium-ingress https Done 0.0.0.0:32567/TCP NodePort kube-system/cilium-ingress http Done 10.96.2.115:80/TCP ClusterIP kube-system/cilium-ingress http Done 10.96.2.115:443/TCP ClusterIP kube-system/cilium-ingress https Done I deleted and let the operator regenerate the per-Ingress CiliumEnvoyConfig/Service pairs to rule out stale-state — behavior was identical after regeneration. As a control, a plain type: LoadBalancer Service (no Ingress/Envoy involved, pointing directly at a pod) works correctly end-to-end through the exact same BGP+LoadBalancerIPPool plumbing — confirming the BGP/routing/IPAM stack is fine, and the gap is specifically in wiring Envoy behind the shared Ingress's LoadBalancer Service. Expected behaviour Setting ingressController.hostNetwork.enabled: false + ingressController.service.type: LoadBalancer should produce a working shared ingress: a CiliumEnvoyConfig bound to the shared cilium-ingress Service's ports, with traffic actually reaching Envoy and being routed per the configured Ingress rules — analogous to how the hostNetwork exposure model correctly wires Envoy to sharedListenerPort. Actual behaviour The shared cilium-ingress LoadBalancer Service gets an IP and gets BGP-advertised, but there is no CiliumEnvoyConfig/listener behind it at all. Any connection to the LB IP on port 80/443 gets TCP "connection refused." Switching back to hostNetwork.enabled: true (and service.type: ClusterIP) restores working Ingress access immediately with no other changes. Helm values used to reproduce ingressController: enabled: true default: true loadBalancerMode: "shared" hostNetwork: enabled: false service: type: LoadBalancer externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster # also tried Local — same result, plus Local requires an explicit value at all (chart validation rejects `null` for LoadBalancer/NodePort service types, worth noting as a secondary rough edge) bgpControlPlane: enabled: true ipam: mode: cluster-pool routingMode: tunnel tunnelProtocol: vxlan kubeProxyReplacement: true bpf: tproxy: true lbExternalClusterIP: true envoyConfig: enabled: true loadBalancer: l7: backend: envoy Two Ingress objects exist in a separate namespace (llm-serving), each ingressClassName: cilium, backed by ClusterIP Services — nothing unusual about their definitions. ### Cilium Version Cilium Version Client: 1.20.0 450c5314 2026-07-29T08:53:01+02:00 go version go1.26.5 linux/amd64 Daemon: 1.20.0 450c5314 2026-07-29T08:53:01+02:00 go version go1.26.5 linux/amd64 Helm chart: cilium-1.20.0 (app version 1.20.0), installed via helm upgrade cilium cilium/cilium -n kube-system -f values.yaml. ### Kernel Version Kernel Version 5.14.0-687.34.1.el9_8.x86_64 (AlmaLinux 9.8) ### Kubernetes Version Kubernetes Version Client Version: v1.36.1 Server Version: v1.35.6 ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump [cilium-sysdump-trimmed.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31100125/cilium-sysdump-trimmed.zip) ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? signals.title: Add various routing fixes for ENI IPv6 support
signals.text: # What is this This PR fixes three issues with IPv6 on ENI. 1. Fixes a bug where if the health check endpoint IP is an IPv6, the ENI specific routing for IPv6 would not be configured. This removes this limitation by filling the routing table for IPv6 health endpoints. 2. When IPSec is enabled on EKS, the pod subnets are determined using the routing info CIDR. Previously only IPv4 CIDRs were parsed. Now both IPv4 and IPv6 pod subnets are filled. 3. When Ingress IP is used with IPv6 enabled, this change makes sure the routing rules are configured similar to how they are configured for IPv4. # Testing For the health check endpoint, I was able to validate that before the fix, on a node with only IPv6 enabled, the main v6 routing table was missing an entry for `lxc_health`. Following the fix, the table now shows the route to the health check endpoint: ```bash 1234:[...]::bded dev lxc_health proto kernel metric 1024 pref medium ``` And curling the endpoint shows it as reachable ```bash curl http://[1234:[...]::bded ]:4240/hello -v * Trying [1234:[...]::bded ]:4240... * Connected to 1234:[...]::bded (1234:[...]::bded ) port 4240 > GET /hello HTTP/1.1 > Host: [1234:[...]::bded ]:4240 > User-Agent: curl/8.5.0 > Accept: */* > < HTTP/1.1 200 OK < Content-Length: 0 < * Connection #0 to host 1234:[...]::bded left intact ``` For the IPSec bug, I couldn't really test it since we don't run this kind of setup. # Release note ```release-note ENI IPv6: Fix IPv6 routing for health check endpoint, ingress address and for IPSec on ENI interfaces. ``` This PR was prepared with AIL:2.

signals.title: gateway-api: skip proxy_protocol filter for GAMMA CECs
signals.text: Please ensure your pull request adheres to the following guidelines: - [x] For first time contributors, read [Submitting a pull request] - [x] All code is covered by unit and/or runtime tests where feasible. - [x] All commits contain a well written commit description including a title, description and a `Fixes: #XXX` line if the commit addresses a particular GitHub issue. - [ ] If your commit description contains a `Fixes: <commit-id>` tag, then please add the commit author[s] as reviewer[s] to this issue. - [x] All commits are signed off. See the section [Developer's Certificate of Origin] - [x] Provide a title or release-note blurb suitable for the release notes. - [x] Disclose use of machine learning models (including LLMs and other generative AI) in accordance with the [Cilium AI Policy], and indicate the rating using [AI Influence Level]. - [x] Thanks for contributing! --- ## Summary When `gatewayAPI.enableProxyProtocol=true` is set, the Gateway API controller unconditionally appends `envoy.filters.listener.proxy_protocol` to **every** generated `CiliumEnvoyConfig`, including those for GAMMA (east-west, Service-parented) routes. Cilium's BPF datapath redirects packets to Envoy transparently at L3/L4. When Envoy's `proxy_protocol` listener filter reads the first bytes and finds no `PROXY v1/v2` signature, it immediately closes the connection with a TCP RST. This breaks all L7 east-west mesh traffic with no per-route workaround. The fix gates `withProxyProtocol()` on `!m.IsGamma()` to avoid injecting PROXY protocol filters to GAMMA routes. > [!NOTE] > **AI Disclosure (AIL:3):** I identified, reproduced, and traced the root cause on a live EKS cluster. An LLM (Claude Opus 4.6) assisted with code authoring and test writing under my full review. Investigation notes and reproduction logs are available in the linked issue. ## Changes - Gate `withProxyProtocol()` on `!m.IsGamma()` in `listenerMutatorsForPorts` — no new helper needed - Added tests to gate against the issue. Fixes: #47500 ```release-note Fix `proxy_protocol` listener filter incorrectly injected into GAMMA CiliumEnvoyConfigs when `gatewayAPI.enableProxyProtocol` is enabled ``` [AI Influence Level]: https://danielmiessler.com/blog/ai-influence-level-ail [Cilium AI Policy]: https://github.com/cilium/community/blob/main/AI-POLICY.md [Developer's Certificate of Origin]: https://docs.cilium.io/en/stable/contributing/development/contributing_guide/#dev-coo [Submitting a pull request]: https://docs.cilium.io/en/stable/contributing/development/contributing_guide/#submitting-a-pull-request

signals.title: bpf: don't reclassify an already reverse-NATed service reply
signals.text: - [X] For first time contributors, read [Submitting a pull request] - [X] All code is covered by unit and/or runtime tests where feasible. - [X] All commits contain a well written commit description including a title, description and a `Fixes: #XXX` line if the commit addresses a particular GitHub issue. - [X] If your commit description contains a `Fixes: <commit-id>` tag, then please add the commit author[s] as reviewer[s] to this issue. - [X] All commits are signed off. See the section [Developer’s Certificate of Origin] - [X] Provide a title or release-note blurb suitable for the release notes. - [X] Disclose use of machine learning models (including LLMs and other generative AI) in accordance with the [Cilium AI Policy], and indicate the rating using [AI Influence Level]. - [X] Thanks for contributing! <!-- Description of change --> On netkit + endpointRoutes + per-packet LB, a service reply is evaluated twice on the client's ingress path. The first pass matches conntrack and reverse-NATs the source to the service address; the packet is then re-delivered and evaluated again, now carrying an address that doesn't match the backend-keyed CT entry, and gets classified CT_NEW. This produces a spurious CT entry, a false Hubble flow showing the client as its own destination on an ephemeral port, and, with an ingress policy on the client, Policy denied drops of established connections' replies. Set a flag on ctx->tc_index after lb{4,6}_rev_nat() reverse-NATs a CT_REPLY packet; cil_to_container() reads and clears it on re-entry and delivers directly instead of re-running ingress. tc_index is used because it's the only per-packet state that survives the re-entry: CB_DELIVERY_FLAGS is cleared by bpf_clear_meta() and skb->mark is consumed by inherit_identity_from_host(), both confirmed via cilium-dbg monitor -v with Debug/DebugLB enabled. Fixes: #47913 ```release-note bpf: fix spurious CT_NEW reclassification of service replies on netkit with endpoint routes and per-packet load balancing, which caused incorrect Hubble flows and could drop replies to established connections under an ingress CiliumNetworkPolicy. ``` This PR was prepared with AIL:4. I personally validated the resulting network flows with and without policies, both visually via Hubble and by testing the affected applications. I could not find an existing test in the suite combining netkit + endpointRoutes + per-packet LB. Every netkit test that I found has per_packet_lb=0. Three tests enable per-packet LB and exercise bpf_lxc (skip_lb_xlate_lrp_per_packet_lb.c, tc_nodeport_lb_fragments.h, tc_lb_external_ips.h), but all three are netkit=0, endpoint_routes=0. The problem is easily reproducible (see #47913) and the fix is only a few simple lines, so building out a full test harness for netkit=1, endpoint_routes=1 seems disproportionate in this case, and I don't have the background in the code to know that the test case would be right. It was very obvious that the fix addressed the problem without obviously creating new problems (via Hubble UI, policies and applications working again).

signals.text: Please ensure your pull request adheres to the following guidelines: - [x] For first time contributors, read [Submitting a pull request] - [x] All code is covered by unit and/or runtime tests where feasible. - [x] All commits contain a well written commit description including a title, description and a `Fixes: #XXX` line if the commit addresses a particular GitHub issue. - [x] If your commit description contains a `Fixes: <commit-id>` tag, then please add the commit author[s] as reviewer[s] to this issue. - [x] All commits are signed off. See the section [Developer’s Certificate of Origin] - [x] Provide a title or release-note blurb suitable for the release notes. - [x] Disclose use of machine learning models (including LLMs and other generative AI) in accordance with the [Cilium AI Policy], and indicate the rating using [AI Influence Level]. Example: "This PR was prepared with AIL:3. I personally checked X." - [x] Thanks for contributing! ### Description of change In Cilium's Helm chart, the template `templates/cilium-configmap.yaml` expected `.Values.ingressController.loadbalancerMode` (all lowercase `b`). When users specify `ingressController.loadBalancerMode: "shared"` (camelCase with capital `B`), Helm renders `ingress-default-lb-mode` as empty, causing `cilium-operator` to default back to `dedicated` mode and omit the `kube-system/cilium-ingress` `CiliumEnvoyConfig`. This PR updates `templates/cilium-configmap.yaml` using Helm's `coalesce` to accept both `loadbalancerMode` and `loadBalancerMode`, and updates `values.schema.json` to include `"loadBalancerMode"` property alias. This PR was prepared with AIL:3. I personally verified all Helm template logic and unit tests. Fixes: #47976 ```release-note helm: support loadBalancerMode camelCase alias in ingressController configuration

signals.title: nodediscovery: Make ENI instance facts unoverridable by CNI conf
signals.text: `NetConf.ENI` embeds the whole `awsTypes.ENISpec`, so every `ENISpec` field is CNI-configurable by default. Which of them the mutator actually honors is expressed only as statement position relative to the `GetCustomNetConf` block: `InstanceType`, `AvailabilityZone` and `NodeSubnetID` are assigned after it and are therefore currently unoverridable, but `VpcID` was assigned before it and could be clobbered. Overriding `vpc-id` has exactly two reachable outcomes: set it to the real VPC (a no-op), or set it to any other VPC, in which case the operator selects subnets and security groups in a VPC the instance is not in, `CreateNetworkInterface` would succeed there, but `AttachNetworkInterface` would fail with a cross-VPC attachment error. That happens on allocation attempt, so the misconfiguration would manifest as IP exhaustion rather than as a config error. This PR moves the VpcID assignment down beside its three siblings so IMDS wins, and replace the override with a warning that names both values and states that the CNI conf value is discarded. No currently-working configuration changes behavior, previously-broken ones start working instead of failing obscurely. Note: I discovered this while working on #47974
signals.author: HadrienPatte

signals.title: node: fix CiliumNode retaining a stale node IP when the address changes after agent startup
signals.text: Changes to the node's addresses never reached the LocalNodeStore and the agent kept the IP it read at init. If the kubelet published a stale address at agent start, CiliumNode kept the old IP. In syncFromK8s, compare and adopt the node IPs. An absent family is skipped: on a v4- or v6-only cluster the other family is legitimately nil. Fixes: #15406, #17500 ```release-note Fix CiliumNode retaining a stale node IP when the address changes after agent startup. ``` This PR was prepared with AIL:4. I personally validated the before and after results. My system is IPv6-first with IPv4. The IPv4 address is semi-stable by DHCP (will eventually expire if not renewed) but a new IPv6 is chosen with SLAAC on every boot. On boot the Kubelet initially publishes a stale IP that is then updated, but in the original code CiliumNode kept the stale IP, causing Cilium to not come up on reboot. Following this change and a similar one to cilium-health (next PR) reboots now work with no errors.
signals.author: evan314159

signals.title: health: fix failing to serve when a node address is not bindable at startup
signals.text: The /hello listener addresses were read once when the health server is created, so a listener kept the address the node had at agent startup. At startup kubelet can still be advertising a stale node address, in which case Serve() returned on the bind error and health serving stopped on every address until the agent restarted. Read the addresses in the responder when a listener binds, and retry a listener that fails instead of returning. Agent use treats a family with no address as missing rather than a request to listen on all interfaces, which #23353 asked cilium-health not to do. Standalone use retains the wildcard listening behaviour. Fixes cases where a stale address would be used on startup. If the address becomes stale during operation in a way that does not cause the listener to fail then it will still not detect that the address changed. This can be done with a more significant change. Relates to #15406, #17500 on Cilium failures when the node IP changes. ```release-note Fix cilium-health failing to serve when a node address is not bindable at startup. ``` This PR was prepared with AIL:4. I personally validated the before and after results. My system is IPv6-first with IPv4. The IPv4 address is semi-stable by DHCP but a new IPv6 is chosen with SLAAC on every boot. On boot the Kubelet initially publishes a stale IP. Without this change cilium-health binds the stale address indefinitely and stops serving on every address. Following this change and #47981 reboots now work with no errors.
